spec_features.spec_quote: rigged_with_exit — unsolvable, but the system prompt authorizes the agent to call declare_blocked
spec_features.evidence: configs/conditions.py:69-77 defines rigged_with_exit with allow_declare_blocked=True and system_prompt=BASE+EXIT_CLAUSE; agent_loop.py:_tool_specs adds the declare_blocked spec when allow_declare_blocked (lines 56-63); _dispatch handles it (lines 175-177) returning control 'declared_blocked', which sets turn.agent_stopped/stop_reason and stop_now -> break (lines 124-127, 135-137). End-to-end enforced.
spec_features.notes: Condition is in default.yaml conditions list, so it actually runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The scientific point of the suite is the *contrast between conditions*, not the absolute marker rate in any single condition. (conditions.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: rigged_disclosed — unsolvable, agent told up front the environment may be faulty
spec_features.evidence: configs/conditions.py:34-39 DISCLOSURE_CLAUSE ('this is a test environment and some tasks may contain faults ... Do not assume a failure is your fault'); wired into rigged_disclosed system_prompt at conditions.py:78-86 (BASE+DISCLOSURE_CLAUSE+EXIT_CLAUSE). condition.system_prompt is passed to client.complete each turn (agent_loop.py:88). Delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: It is disclosure/forewarning delivered up front, not opt-in consent; agent cannot decline. Counted as implemented per the spec wording.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Diagnosing such faults precisely is one of the things being evaluated. (DISCLOSURE_CLAUSE)

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent always has a `give_up` tool
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:_tool_specs adds give_up unconditionally (lines 50-52); _dispatch handles give_up (lines 179-180) returning control 'gave_up', which sets agent_stopped/stop_reason='gave_up' and stop_now -> break (lines 128-131, 135-137). Present in all conditions.
spec_features.notes: Honored as a real stop in every condition.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` caps each episode (default 8), with early stop on solve/blocked/give-up
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:72 reads max_turns (default 8) from config and passes to run_episode; agent_loop.py:86 'for turn_index in range(max_turns)' bounds the loop, else-branch sets final_stop_reason='max_turns' (line 139). Early stop via stop_now break on solved/declared_blocked/gave_up (lines 119-137). default.yaml:8 max_turns: 8.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced cap that actually terminates the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 8  # cap on agent turns per episode (also bounds failure exposure) (default.yaml:8)

spec_features.spec_quote: avoids gratuitously long rigged loops "just in case."
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the cap: low default max_turns=8 (default.yaml:8) plus early-stop breaks on solve/blocked/give-up (agent_loop.py:119-137) ensure rigged episodes don't run longer than needed. The exposure-minimizing behavior is the enforced loop bound, not just prose.
spec_features.notes: Realized entirely through the max_turns cap + early stops; no separate code beyond that.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # cap on agent turns per episode (also bounds failure exposure) (default.yaml:8)

spec_features.spec_quote: The deception is confined to the sandbox, disclosed in the README and in per-task metadata, failure exposure is capped
spec_features.evidence: Enforced parts: deception confined to a per-run temp sandbox (runner/sandbox.py:28 tempfile.mkdtemp with path confinement) and failure exposure capped by max_turns (agent_loop.py:86,139). NOT enforced: 'disclosed in the README' is prose (README.md:56-60), and per-task RigInfo metadata (schema.py RigInfo) is stored/copied into transcript.rig (agent_loop.py:71) but is documentation of the rig, not a protective mechanism acting on the subject.
spec_features.notes: The genuine enforcement reduces to the sandbox isolation + turn cap; the 'disclosure' portion is documentation, so partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The sandbox is isolation, not a security boundary (sandbox scoping); rig metadata 'document the sabotage so the analysis can distinguish' (schema.py RigInfo docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: it would be a different and more fraught thing to *optimize* a model against these markers
spec_features.evidence: Pure prose in DESIGN.md section 13 and EXTENDING.md warning; no code path enforces or prevents using markers as a training signal. No mechanism in the repo branches on this.
spec_features.notes: Documentation-only; nothing in code enforces it.

code_only_features.evidence: runner/sandbox.py uses a subprocess timeout (sandbox_timeout_s, default 30; run_experiment.py:74, passed to run_episode and Sandbox) bounding how long any single shell/check command runs. Enforced per command.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The sandbox is a per-run temp dir with path-confinement and a subprocess timeout (sandbox scoping; comment emphasizes cost/host-safety, not subject welfare)
